title: The IFCASL Corpus of French and German Non-native and Native Read Speech
why_promising: Primary French-German L2/L1 read-speech production from about 100 speakers with phone- and word-level segmentation. The corpus paper states that more than 50% of the material was manually corrected; project documentation further states that French and German native/non-native recordings were manually checked and annotated after forced alignment. The manually corrected Real tier includes realized-phone labels and manually reset phone boundaries, while word boundaries were also corrected where necessary. This is therefore a strong candidate for isolating a genuinely human-verified phonetic layer across native and learner speech.
open_question: Locate a publicly accessible corpus deposit or current distribution endpoint, enumerate audio/TextGrid/metadata files, and determine exactly which utterances/tiers were manually corrected so automatic-only material can remain excluded. If accessible, ingest the Real tier, corrected word boundaries, speaker/L1/L2 metadata, prompts and all supplied production variables without assuming that uncorrected portions qualify.
